name: Hong Kong
summary_text: Hong Kong: own legal system under Basic Law: no criminalisation, ordinance protections and an active court arena; NSL-era chill on open activism; Pride continues under heavier police conditions. Scored as a dependent jurisdiction: the parent framework governs what a visitor encounters, plus local society and enforcement. Score re-anchored 2026-09-24: China (0.40) plus a local delta of +0.18. This jurisdiction was not covered by the dedicated state/province research passes.

sources.title: Thai transgender YouTuber alleges sexist treatment at Chinese airport | Thaiger
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This article is about a Thai trans YouTuber's treatment at a mainland Chinese airport, not Hong Kong; included as regional context.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying NYT investigation covers transgender 'conversion' practices in China - regional context for Hong Kong.

AP (Feb 2023): 'Hong Kong transgender men win appeal over status change' — the Court of Final Appeal rules full sex-reassignment surgery should not be a prerequisite for changing the gender marker on official identity cards, a far-reaching win in the Henry Tse case.

sources.title: Hong Kong rules transgender people need surgery to change legal gender | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Feb 2019): Hong Kong's High Court ruled against three trans men (Henry Tse, Q and R) seeking legal gender change without full confirmation surgery - Judge Thomas Au called full surgery the 'only objectively ascertainable criterion'; the men had already changed legal gender in Britain; lawyers called the requirement 'out of proportion'.

sources.title: HSBC's rainbow lions: Can we have our homophobia back please? | Hong Kong Free Press HKFP
sources.claim_summary: Hong Kong Free Press (Dec 2016): opinion piece on HSBC's rainbow-lion statues and the homophobic backlash they provoked - the social climate around corporate LGBT visibility in Hong Kong.

sources.title: CACV000317A/2005 LEUNG T C WILLIAM ROY v. SECRETARY FOR JUSTICE
sources.claim_summary: Hong Kong Court of Appeal judgment (Leung TC William Roy v Secretary for Justice, CACV317/2005, Sept 2006): landmark ruling on whether the Crimes Ordinance's buggery provisions unjustifiably discriminate against gay men - the court examined whether facially neutral laws can be discriminatory; key precedent for equal age of consent.
